title: Five names that all look like a_b under naive concatenation stay five distinct fields
rationale: The direct probe of FlattenedPath injectivity. The document contains a name with a raw backslash, a name that is literally the encoder OWN OUTPUT for a different name, the name a_b itself, the two-level path a.b, and a name ending in a backslash. If escape order is wrong or the decoder escapes-nothing branch fires wrongly, at least two of these collapse into each other.
catchesBugClass: Escape-ordering bugs and double-unescaping. Specifically catches escaping the separator before the escape character, which would make a name that already contains a backslash indistinguishable from a name that was escaped once.
cannotCatch: It only probes the single-character default separator. It also cannot catch anything downstream of decode - a name here could decode perfectly and still be dropped by processArrays.

predicted.detail: The five encode to distinct keys and each decodes back to its exact source name. Escaping the backslash first is what keeps the pre-encoded lookalike from decoding as the two-level path.
